claim: Digital media and software arrive as wireless files.
originalWording: Digital media and software arrive as wireless files.

sources.title: How My Predictions Are Faring — Ray Kurzweil
sources.locator: The Computer Itself, prediction 9, printed p. 18

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source and full record for attribution limits.

reference.criterion: Books, music, video and software can routinely be delivered as downloadable wireless data without a physical carrier.
reference.rationale: Kindle, iTunes and the App Store supplied the listed media/software functions before the deadline. Continued paper-book or disc sales do not refute routine file distribution; the claim does not require every purchase to be digital.

evidence.title: Introducing Amazon Kindle
evidence.note: Wireless-delivery section and Books, Blogs, Magazines and Newspapers section. The 2007 Kindle release describes EVDO delivery of books and periodicals without a computer or Wi-Fi hotspot. Evidence limits: This establishes available functions; it does not establish the share of all media delivered wirelessly.

evidence.title: iTunes Store tops over five billion songs sold
evidence.note: Opening sales paragraph and catalogue descriptions. Apple reports five billion song downloads and more than 50,000 daily movie rentals/purchases by June 2008. Evidence limits: These are digital-distribution counts, not wireless-only transactions or all-media market share.

evidence.title: iPhone App Store downloads top 10 million
evidence.note: Wireless-download paragraph and cellular/Wi-Fi distribution paragraph. The July 2008 release explicitly describes direct app downloads over cellular networks and Wi-Fi. Evidence limits: The same release also describes USB syncing; wireless availability does not mean cables had disappeared.
